documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
35 y/o man here to set up primary care. Previous office is no longer taking adults on his plan. Feels well overall.

PMH: Seasonal allergies since his late teens/early 20s, worse April-May and again September. Takes cetirizine 10 mg on the days he needs it, which is most of the spring. Mild acne off and on since high school, mostly forehead and jaw; never used a prescription for it and isn't bothered enough to want one.
PSH: none.
Meds: cetirizine 10 mg daily PRN.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FH: Dad has type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure. Mom has hypothyroidism and seasonal allergies. An uncle on his father's side was on dialysis; family never learned the cause.
SH: Teaches algebra and precalculus at the high school. Lives in Amherst. Never smoked. A drink or two on weekends. No drug use. Coaches the math team.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: Well appearing. HEENT: mild pale nasal turbinates, oropharynx clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Ext warm, no swelling. Skin: a few small comedones and papules on forehead, no cysts or scarring.

Assessment/plan:
1. Health maintenance. Baseline CMP, CBC, lipids, UA. One-time HIV and hep C screens; he agrees. Tetanus and COVID per prior records, will confirm when they arrive.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis, controlled with as-needed cetirizine. Continue.
3. Mild acne. No treatment wanted.
4. FH of kidney disease in an uncle, unknown cause. Baseline creatinine and UA today.

RTC for a physical in about a year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Andre, everything from your first visit came back normal: kidney and liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol and urine. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

documents.body:
Video from his classroom after dismissal. Four days of stuffy nose, sore throat and dry cough, started the first week back with students. Tmax 99.8 at home. No shortness of breath, no facial pain, no ear pain. Eating and drinking normally. Home COVID antigen negative x2.

On video: speaking full sentences, congested voice, no distress, no increased work of breathing.

Impression: viral upper respiratory infection.
Plan: supportive care, fluids, saline rinses, acetaminophen or ibuprofen as needed, honey for the cough. Antibiotics not indicated. Call if fever above 101, breathing trouble, or not better in 10 days.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: legs swelling, tired.

He noticed his socks leaving deep marks in early August, before school started, and figured it was the heat. Swelling in both ankles and shins has kept up since, worse by evening, and the last couple of weeks his eyes look puffy when he wakes up. More tired than usual, napping after school, which isn't like him. Pants a little tight at the waist. The cold from two weeks ago is gone. Urine looks foamy to him. No dyspnea, no orthopnea, no chest pain, no rash, no joint pain. No new meds or supplements, no NSAIDs beyond a few doses with the cold.

Exam: Up 4 kg from June. Mild puffiness of both lower lids. JVP not elevated. Heart regular, no gallop. Lungs clear, no crackles. Abdomen soft, no fluid wave. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin bilaterally, symmetric, calves nontender.

UA in office: protein 4+, blood negative.

Assessment: new edema with heavy proteinuria, picture of nephrotic syndrome until proven otherwise. Cardiac and liver causes unlikely on exam. FH of an uncle with ESRD.

Plan:
- CMP, lipids, CBC sent today.
- Called nephrology directly; they can see him next Monday 10/3.
- Low-salt diet in the meantime, legs up in the evening.
- Avoid ibuprofen/naproxen.
- He knows to go to the ED for breathlessness, chest pain or much less urine.

documents.title: Lab results call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt on his lunch break per PCP. Albumin low and cholesterol high, consistent with the protein loss in his urine; kidney function (creatinine) normal, blood counts normal. Nephrology appt confirmed Mon 10/3 at 2:30, he has arranged coverage for his last classes. Swelling about the same. Reinforced low salt, no NSAIDs. He verbalized understanding.

documents.title: Nephrology Consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group, new consultation. Received by fax 10/5/2022.

Reason: edema and heavy proteinuria, referred by his primary care physician.

HPI: 37-year-old teacher with roughly two months of tiredness and swelling of both legs. He had a viral respiratory illness about three weeks ago, managed by his PCP with supportive care, now over. Describes foamy urine. No hematuria, rash, arthralgia, or NSAID use beyond a few doses.

PMH: allergic rhinitis, mild acne. Meds: cetirizine 10 mg as needed. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with type 2 DM and HTN; mother with hypothyroidism and seasonal allergies; paternal uncle with ESRD, cause unknown.
SH: never smoker, light weekend alcohol, high school math teacher.

Exam: Vitals within normal limits. Periorbital edema present. Lower extremities with 2+ pitting edema bilaterally. Cardiopulmonary exam unremarkable. No rash.

Data: Urinalysis with 4+ protein; microscopy shows oval fat bodies with Maltese-cross pattern under polarized light, no RBC casts. Serum albumin 2.5 g/dL. Total cholesterol 300 mg/dL. Creatinine 1.0 mg/dL. Spot urine protein/creatinine 6.8 g/g.

Impression: nephrotic syndrome in a young adult with preserved filtration. Differential includes minimal change disease, FSGS and membranous nephropathy; a tissue diagnosis will guide therapy.

Plan: percutaneous kidney biopsy scheduled 10/13. Sodium restriction. Avoid NSAIDs. Will see after pathology returns.

cc: primary care physician

reports.text:
Specimen: native kidney, left, percutaneous needle core biopsy (ultrasound guided, 16-gauge, two cores).
Light microscopy: adequate sample with multiple glomeruli for evaluation. Scattered glomeruli show segmental areas of sclerosis with hyalinosis; the remaining glomeruli appear unremarkable. Tubules and interstitium without significant change. Vessels unremarkable.
Immunofluorescence: negative for IgG, IgA, IgM, C3 and C1q; no immune complex deposits.
Electron microscopy: no electron-dense deposits identified.
reports.conclusion: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. No immune complex or complement deposition.

documents.title: Kidney biopsy pathology received

documents.body: Pathology report from the outside hospital (kidney biopsy 10/13/22) received by fax and scanned. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Percutaneous Kidney Biopsy
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Outside procedure note, received 10/24/2022. Indication: nephrotic syndrome. Consent obtained. Prone position, left lower pole localized by ultrasound, local anesthetic, two cores with 16-gauge automated device. No immediate complications. Observed 4 hours, hemoglobin stable, urine clear, discharged home with instructions.

medications.sig: Take 3 tablets (60 mg) by mouth every morning with food
Take 1 tablet by mouth every morning

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology follow-up, visit 10/24/2022, received 10/26/2022.

Biopsy reviewed with patient: focal segmental glomerulosclerosis without immune deposits. With the full nephrotic picture and no secondary cause found, we are treating as primary disease.

Still has ankle and shin edema. No complications after the biopsy. Vitals unremarkable.

Plan:
1. Prednisone 60 mg each morning, to continue at full dose until remission or up to about 16 weeks, then a slow taper. Reviewed effects on mood, sleep, appetite and glucose.
2. Losartan 25 mg daily for proteinuria; BMP in 2 weeks.
3. Furosemide 20 mg daily for the swelling, to stop once edema clears.
4. 2 g sodium diet.
5. Return in 6-8 weeks with urine protein/creatinine.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN, prednisone, losartan, furosemide. Allergies: NKDA.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after his kidney biopsy and nephrology visit. Diagnosis is FSGS; nephrology started prednisone 60 mg, losartan 25 mg and furosemide 20 mg one week ago. He has read a lot and came in with a page of questions, mostly whether this is what his uncle had and whether he can keep teaching. Swelling a bit better with the water pill. Tolerating prednisone so far.

Exam: puffiness around eyes less. Lungs clear. 1+ pitting edema at the ankles. 

A/P:
1. FSGS with nephrotic syndrome, on steroids per nephrology. We went through what is and isn't known about familial kidney disease; the rest of that conversation belongs with nephrology. He can work. Hand hygiene in class while immunosuppressed; flu vaccine today. BMP today for the 2-week potassium/creatinine check nephrology asked for, results to them.
2. Allergic rhinitis: cetirizine PRN.
Next: physical next summer, sooner with any fever or worse swelling.

documents.title: RE: Flu going around school
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good that you got the flu shot. A mask in class during this stretch is reasonable, and wash hands before eating. If you get a fever or body aches, message or call the same day so we can test and treat early.

Exam: no periorbital or leg edema. BP normal.
Urine protein/creatinine 2.1 g/g, down from 6.8. Chemistry acceptable.

Plan: stop furosemide. Continue prednisone 60 mg and losartan 25 mg. Recheck in 8 weeks.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit 4/1/2024, received 4/2/2024.

38-year-old man, history of FSGS in remission off treatment, presenting with fever and generally feeling unwell. Cold symptoms for about 10 days, seen by video by his PCP last week; today worse, with chills, aches and fatigue. Mild cough. No dyspnea, chest pain, dysuria, abdominal pain, headache or neck stiffness. No rash.
Meds: cetirizine PRN. NKDA. Never smoker.

Triage: T 38.7, HR 112, BP 124/74, RR 20, SpO2 97% RA.
Exam: ill-appearing but nontoxic. Oropharynx mildly erythematous. Neck supple. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Skin without rash.

Results: WBC 13.6. CRP 87 mg/L. Chemistry with normal creatinine. UA no protein, no infection. CXR clear. Blood cultures x2 sent.

Course: 2 L IV fluids, acetaminophen 1 g. Repeat T 37.4, HR 88, feeling much better, tolerating PO.

Impression: systemic inflammatory response following a viral upper respiratory infection; no bacterial source identified.
Disposition: home. PCP follow-up in 2-3 days; we will call with any positive culture. Return for persistent fever, breathing trouble, confusion or new swelling.

Exam: afebrile, HR in the 70s. Throat clear, lungs clear, heart regular. No edema.

About a week of feeling run down with low-grade fevers, body aches and nasal congestion. Some pressure across the cheeks. No shortness of breath.

events.reason: painful blistering rash with mucosal involvement

medications.reason: suspected cause of toxic epidermal necrolysis

reports.text: Portable AP view. Lungs clear. No effusion or pneumothorax. Cardiomediastinal silhouette normal.

Specimen: skin, upper chest, punch biopsy at the edge of a blister. Sections show full-thickness necrosis of the epidermis with subepidermal separation. Sparse superficial perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate in the dermis.
reports.conclusion: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with sparse lymphocytic infiltrate, consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis in the clinical setting.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: ICU Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
Regional hospital, critical care service. Admitted 10/9/2025, discharged 10/30/2025. Received 11/3/2025.

Presentation: 40-year-old man, FSGS in remission and a prior systemic inflammatory response episode (2024), seen at urgent care 10/1 for an upper respiratory illness and started on amoxicillin. A week of malaise, low-grade fevers and aches. A few days after starting the antibiotic, redness and stinging of the face and chest, then painful, spreading darker areas that blistered and peeled. Severe mouth soreness, burning and swelling of the eyes so he could hardly open them, difficulty drinking, and pain with urination. Home meds: cetirizine as needed, amoxicillin. Allergies on arrival: none known.

Admission exam: T 38.9, HR 124. Uncomfortable and distressed. Face and upper trunk with confluent dusky erythematous patches, flaccid bullae and areas of sloughing; Nikolsky sign positive. Oral mucosa with erosions and hemorrhagic crusts on the lips. Similar lesions periocular and genital.

Data: WBC 3.3 (mild leukopenia). ALT 118, AST 96. Creatinine normal. Chest x-ray unremarkable. Skin punch biopsy: full-thickness epidermal necrosis with sparse lymphocytic infiltrate.

Diagnosis: toxic epidermal necrolysis; amoxicillin judged the culprit (only new drug, typical timing).

Hospital course: amoxicillin stopped on arrival. ICU-level supportive care: fluid resuscitation, warmed room, non-adherent dressings and wound care with the burn nursing team, pain control, nutrition support, urinary catheter for the genital involvement for the first part of the stay. Ophthalmology saw him daily for the eyes. Mouth care with bland rinses. Fever settled. No infection identified. Skin progressively re-epithelialized; mucosa healed enough to eat by week three. Creatinine stayed at his baseline throughout. Liver enzymes back to normal by 10/29; white count recovered.

Allergy added: AMOXICILLIN (toxic epidermal necrolysis). Avoid amoxicillin and related penicillins.

Discharge meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN.
Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; ophthalmology and dermatology clinic appointments made.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after hospital discharge yesterday. He's home. Skin tender in spots but no new blisters; eating soft foods. Eyes comfortable. No fever. Medication list reviewed: cetirizine only. Amoxicillin allergy added to our chart pending the summary. PCP visit Wed 11/5 at 3:30 confirmed.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three weeks in the ICU at the regional hospital for toxic epidermal necrolysis after amoxicillin from urgent care (summary received 11/3, reviewed in full). Home since 10/30.

Today: skin no longer weeping, a few areas still pink and tender on the chest. Eating regular food now. Eyes feel normal. Urinating without pain. No fever. Tired, but walking daily. Planning to go back to school in a couple of weeks; asked for a work note.

Exam: afebrile, vitals stable. Face and upper chest with pink, newly healed skin, no bullae, no erosions, no drainage. Lips healed. Conjunctivae quiet. Lungs clear. 

A/P:
1. TEN due to amoxicillin, healing well. Allergy entered: amoxicillin, severe, high criticality; advised to avoid all penicillins and to tell every prescriber and pharmacist. Wallet card printed. Ophthalmology 11/19 and dermatology 12/3 already booked.
2. Labs: CMP and CBC to confirm the liver and counts stayed normal.
3. FSGS: creatinine was normal throughout the admission; nephrology letter to follow at their annual visit.
4. Work note for return 11/17.
RTC after the specialist visits, around the new year.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology letter, visit 11/19/2025, received 11/21/2025.

Seen in follow-up after inpatient care for ocular involvement of toxic epidermal necrolysis. Asymptomatic.
Vision 20/20 each eye. Lids and lashes normal. Conjunctivae quiet without symblepharon or scarring. Corneas clear, no staining. Tear film adequate.
Impression: ocular surface healed, no sequelae.
Plan: no further routine follow-up needed; return for redness, pain or vision change.
Allergies: amoxicillin (TEN).

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology letter, visit 12/3/2025, received 12/5/2025.

Follow-up after toxic epidermal necrolysis attributed to amoxicillin, October 2025. Back at work, no complaints.
Exam: previously affected skin of face, chest and upper back fully re-epithelialized; no blisters, erosions or scarring. Oral and genital mucosa normal. Nails normal. Mild comedonal acne on forehead.
Assessment: TEN, healed.
Recommendations: lifelong avoidance of amoxicillin and other penicillins; allergy documented in all records; consider a medical alert bracelet. Sun protection for the next few months on recently healed skin.

cc: primary care physician

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Winter break visit. Ten weeks out from the TEN admission. Back teaching full time since mid-November. Skin feels normal, no sores, eyes fine. No fevers or infections since. Got through the fall without his usual flu shot because of the hospital stay; wants it today.

Ophthalmology (11/19): eyes healed, no scarring, discharged from their care. Dermatology (12/3): skin healed, avoid penicillins.

Meds: cetirizine 10 mg PRN. Allergies: amoxicillin (TEN).

Exam: well. Skin of face and trunk intact, no erosions or blisters. Oral mucosa normal. Conjunctivae clear. Heart and lungs normal. No ankle edema.

A/P:
1. Toxic epidermal necrolysis, amoxicillin: healed; moved to history. Allergy flagged; he carries the card.
2. FSGS in remission: chemistry, UA and urine albumin today after the hospital stay; results will be copied to them.
3. Flu vaccine given.
4. Allergic rhinitis, mild acne: unchanged.
Physical next summer or early fall.

documents.body: Andre, Friday's results are all normal: kidney function, liver tests, blood counts, and no protein or albumin in the urine. I've sent a copy to nephrology. Happy new year.

documents.title: RE: January labs

documents.body: Best news I've had in a while. Thank you.

documents.title: Nephrology Follow-up
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology note, visit 3/9/2026, received 3/11/2026.

Seen a little early after his October ICU admission for toxic epidermal necrolysis (amoxicillin), now healed. Renal function was preserved through that illness and January labs from his PCP were normal.
Today: no edema, BP normal. Urine protein negative, urine albumin normal, creatinine baseline.
Assessment: FSGS, sustained complete remission, off therapy since 2023.
Plan: yearly follow-up. Allergies: amoxicillin (TEN); avoid penicillins.

cc: primary care physician
